summary.text: A 74-year-old man with cirrhosis due to nonalcoholic steatohepatitis was asymptomatic and had a liver mass found on screening imaging. General and abdominal examination was unremarkable; liver function tests, coagulation profile and the rest of the blood count were normal apart from a low platelet count printed as 70/µL, and AFP was normal. Contrast CT showed a 6.5 cm segment 8 mass with arterial enhancement, washout and LI-RADS category 5; the final diagnosis was large solitary hepatocellular carcinoma (early stage) with preserved liver function and no vascular invasion or extrahepatic metastasis.

After HCC tumor board discussion, TACE was recommended as bridging/downstaging therapy before liver transplantation. The first DEB-TACE session used 150 mg doxorubicin loaded onto two vials of 100-300 µm DC Bead microspheres; the 6-week CT showed partial response, so a second session with 75 mg doxorubicin on one vial was performed, after which CT showed complete response. He was deemed ineligible for transplantation because of advanced age.

At 1 year CT showed continued complete response with faint peripheral hyperdensities suggesting early calcification, and he was actively monitored clinically, with laboratory tests and imaging. At 6 years CT showed sustained complete response with progressive peripheral concentric calcification; the abstract reports remission with preserved liver function over 6 years. The author regards the calcification as a hypothesis-generating imaging observation, and CR by mRECIST preceded it.

summary.text: A 71-year-old man with cirrhosis due to hepatitis C virus was asymptomatic and had a liver mass found on screening imaging. General and abdominal examination was unremarkable; blood count, coagulation profile and liver function tests were normal, but AFP was elevated at 420 ng/mL. Abdominal MRI showed a 6 cm segment 7 mass with arterial enhancement, washout and LI-RADS category 5; the final diagnosis was large solitary hepatocellular carcinoma (early stage) with preserved liver function and no vascular invasion or extrahepatic metastasis.

After HCC tumor board discussion, TACE was recommended as bridging/downstaging therapy before liver transplantation. The first DEB-TACE session used 150 mg doxorubicin loaded onto two vials of 100-300 µm DC Bead microspheres; MRI 8 weeks later showed partial response, so a second session with 75 mg doxorubicin on one vial was performed, after which CT showed complete response. Serum AFP normalized after the second session and remained normal.

At 1 year CT showed continued complete response with faint peripheral hyperdensities consistent with early calcification. He declined liver transplantation because the tumor had achieved CR and entered routine clinical, laboratory and imaging follow-up. At 6 years CT showed sustained complete response with progressive peripheral concentric calcification; the abstract reports remission with preserved liver function over 6 years. The author regards the calcification as a hypothesis-generating imaging observation, and CR by mRECIST preceded it.

article_limitations: Case 1 platelet count is printed "70/µL" and retained literally with an explicit low flag; the unit is probably an omission of the 10^3 multiplier but no correction was applied.

No biopsy/histology, tumor grade, BCLC letter, TNM stage, Child-Pugh class or ECOG is documented; "early stage" and "preserved liver function" are the only staging/reserve statements and the HCC diagnosis rests on LI-RADS 5 imaging.

Dates and exact session intervals are not given; post-second-session CT intervals (4 and 6 weeks) and the anchoring of 1-year/6-year CTs to the second session come from figure captions. Response labels are radiological.

Calcification mechanism (coagulative necrosis/dystrophic) and its role as a late imaging marker are author hypotheses, kept review-only; the cited prior DEB-TACE calcification case is background, not the index patients.

Figure 1 and Figure 2 captions do not name the case; ownership follows the narrative call-outs in b00018 and b00019. Pixel-level description is in the separate visual submission; the caption-layer figure fields remain not_inspected by convention.
